utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Martinovic and Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Before we have the next witness, I would like to remind both parties that this week, we only have three days and two hours because of the other obligations for the Judges. Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The witness who is called to testify now requested the following protective measures: pseudonym and facial distortion. The motivation is that he lives now in the area, and he is an officer of the Armija Federation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Your request is granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And now, about the relevancy of the witness's testimony. First of all, his testimony will go mostly to the background, paragraph 7; superior authority, paragraph 17; general allegations, paragraph 18; count 1, paragraphs 20, 728 [sic], 30, 34(a), (b), (d); counts 2 through 8, paragraphs 35 through 38, 40 through 32 [sic]; counts 9 through 12, paragraph 45, 49, 50; and count 21, paragraph 57.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper the usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down, please. Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Examined by Mr. Poriouvaev:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, good morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your request for protective measures has been granted by the -- by this Trial Chamber. Now you have a pseudonym. You will be called "Witness OO" in the courtroom, and you have also facial distortion, which means that your face will not be seen on the screen or the monitor. And at some point, maybe I will ask the Trial Chamber to consider some questions in private session. And I would like to warn you, Witness, when you want to give us some name, to first consult with me, just not to reveal the identity of people whose identity should be protected. Okay. Now you will be given a sheet of paper with a name, date of birth. Don't read it aloud, just read it to yourself. If everything is all right with your first name, full name, and the spelling is also right, you may say "yes," and we understand that no mistakes were made.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, in June 1992, you were mobilised into the HVO, and until July 1993, you were a member of the 2nd Company, 3rd battalion of the Knez Domagoj Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I will lead the witness through some irrelevant issues now, straight to the points that are of most interest to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So then you were arrested. When did it happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes. I was arrested on the 4th of July, 1993 in the place called Rotimlja, the municipality of Stolac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will not ask you the details about the circumstances of this arrest because this Trial Chamber has already had some witnesses who testified to the fact. So I would ask you some maybe questions relevant to this arrest and relevant to our case. First of all, did they explain to you somehow why you and your colleagues - I mean other soldiers - were arrested? What was the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: The reason was probably that we were Muslims. Because from day one, we were members of the HVO. They didn't explain anything to us, apart from saying that we would be put away for a while. And then they transferred us on trucks to the former JNA barracks of Gabela where there was no place for us. So they returned us to another former JNA barracks, which later became the camp of Dretelj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would ask you to speak a little bit slower because your answers, responses, will be translated simultaneously into several languages. And wait, please, for my answer and wait a little, just maybe a second, and then give your response. Could you shortly inform the Trial Chamber about the conditions of detention in Dretelj camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Right. The conditions were the same as for cattle. We lay on bare concrete. We didn't even have enough water, let alone food. From the 13th to the 17th of that month, we were given no food and no water. We were about 400 men, and we only could go to toilet in a hangar. That's the only toilet we had. And we could get hold of very little food, and we ate in the same place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was in charge of Dretelj detention facilities? I don't mean a personality. If you don't know, you don't know. Just I'm interested in administrative or military body that was in charge of these facilities.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Members of the HVO were in charge, or more precisely, the military police of the Knez Domagoj Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you were taken to Heliodrom; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: That's correct. Around the 19th of July, in the afternoon hours, we were loaded onto trucks and took us by the road from Capljina to Citluk to Mostar to Heliodrom. In Heliodrom, they made us jump off the trucks, holding us, propping us by the arms. Two lines of military policemen and the HVO were waiting for us there. And each of us was hit at least once on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which building were you placed in Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: They put us up in a former school building. It used to be the aviation high school of the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit P20.4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at the picture, and to the best of your recollection, what does this picture depict? Do you recognise the place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes. This is the Heliodrom camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you just point out the building you were placed in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean the former school building? Yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know Mostar very well, but I know I spent four days in this building, before we were transferred to the sports hall, also at the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this sports hall in the picture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. I would like you to mark the building you were kept in with a number "1."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And for the record, this was a building under number "1," where Witness OO was kept in the beginning of his detention in Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know for what purposes were the buildings in this picture designed for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: It used to be a barracks of the former army, the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean during the war, during the time when you were detained there, not before.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: During the war, it was built up. There were about 10.000 Bosniaks, Muslims, there. It was a camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see any military units deployed in Heliodrom area, in Heliodrom itself and close to Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes. At the Heliodrom, there were troops who called themselves Bruno Busic. And while I was there at a later stage, the Zagreb Tigers arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, Witness, just -- I would like you to describe briefly the conditions of detention in Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: The conditions were not appropriate for humans. We didn't have enough food. Again, we lay on the parquet. They took us to perform hard labour and act constantly as human shields. We got our share of beatings every day from everyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just let us dwell a little bit on labour that you were involved.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you involved in such kind of labour outside Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes. I went to do forced labour every day from the HUM hill all the way up to Bune. The longest stretch that I did was 13 days, and that was in Santiceva Street and around the Health Centre on the Bulevar. More precisely, at Stela's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of job did you perform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: We filled sacks with sands. We dug all sorts of canals. We went ahead of lines to put up some sort of fortification shields, shelters, trenches, to carry things from Muslim-owned flats to their quarters, that is, the quarters of the members of the HVO. And those things were household appliances, TV sets, VCRs, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to clarify some points. Was the unit on Bulevar, as you called it, Stela's unit, the only one for which you performed some kind of labour as mentioned by you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: On the Bulevar, Stela's unit was the only one that I worked for. And on other locations, Stela's unit was not present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What other units were present at other locations, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: In Santiceva Street, there were members of the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... of that unit of the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you know that they were from Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I know that because at one point, somewhere in the beginning of August, I was working on Santiceva Street, and I was talking to a man who introduced himself to me as a senior officer of the Croatian army and who asked me why I was in prison. On their sleeves, they had the sign of "HV" visible displayed. It was only later on that both on their sleeves and their vehicles they added the letter "O" to make it read "HVO."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's talk a little bit about Bulevar. First of all, you just talked -- told the Trial Chamber about a person whose -- who you called Stela. Did you know a person with this name before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I didn't know him before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the first time you were taken to his unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes. It happened immediately after our arrival at the Heliodrom, that is, somewhere between the 24th and the 25th of July. I remember well that we arrived there. We were 20 to 30 men per group. He would line us all up outside his command, which was a red building. On such occasions, most of the men would be mistreated by Stela. He would call us extremists, fundamentalists, and various other names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he introduce himself somehow to prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes. He always introduced himself. He would say, "My name is Stela." And he was the terror of everyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you describe his physical appearance as you saw him in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: When I saw him, he had short hair. He was stocky, not tall, built like a boxer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did prisoners call him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: The prisoners called him "Mr. Colonel," "Commander," things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he really wearing a colonel uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: He had no insignia then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember any other commanders within Stela's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Within Stela's unit, I remember there is only one.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: "There were men like Marinko Dolma, Ernest Takac, also known as Brada, and those are the only men I remember."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you remember two men, yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go down to Bulevar now. Was Stela's unit the only one deployed on Bulevar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes, that was the only unit deployed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Initially, it was called "ATG Stela Mrmak." Later, I don't remember its official name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which positions were held on Bulevar by Vinko -- by Mrmak unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: It held positions around the health centre.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness also said that the unit was named after his dog.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Near the fountain which was pretty much destroyed. However, a portion of it was still standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they occupy some buildings along Bulevar?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Sorry, could we get some repetition of an interpretation that came late? If you look at your -- "Interpreter: The witness also said the unit was named after his dog." Could we get some clarification on that? It just seems juxtaposed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And we have some problem in the English channel. We hear the B/C/S translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Maybe I should switch off my mike, or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't know. You may try that, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Witness OO, you just stated that the unit run by Stela was called after his dog's name. Would you give an explanation with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes. I can explain that. Here on the sleeve, there was an insignia which read, "ATG Stela," and there was another word next to it, "Mrmak," which was the name of a very big dog.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see that dog?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like Witness OO shown Exhibit number 14.4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, take a look at this picture. And my first question will be: Do you remember the places on Bulevar you were working for Stela's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes. These are the positions in question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And what was there in that building you have just shown?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: They were -- there were their lines. There was nothing actually on those lines because everything had been destroyed. The only thing we could find there were parts of tablets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever work in some other buildings along Bulevar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: No. I didn't work in any other buildings except on those occasions where -- when we had to carry things all around Mostar, that is, on the other side, when they were doing the looting, and when we had to carry the household appliances for them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who commanded you when you were, say, looting things from Muslim houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Sometimes the orders were issued directly by Stela and then, on other occasions, his soldiers -- by his soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as I understand, Witness OO, you are not from Mostar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So may I suggest that you don't know the area of Mostar very well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: No, I don't know it very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While talking about looting, looting in other areas, do you mean the areas that were located far away from Bulevar or close to it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I think that they were located far away from the Bulevar, such as the part in the vicinity of the new hospital in Mostar. That is the area that I have in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was happening on the confrontation line itself on the Bulevar itself? I mean while you were performing a job there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Sometimes we were made to be -- act as human shield. It happened sometime in mid-September; between the 17th and the 19th of August, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: September or August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question was leading regarding the date. But the witness has already answered, so I withdraw my objection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to clarify. "Sometimes we were made to act as human shields. It happened sometime in mid-September; between the 17th and the 19th of August." That was my question, because once we have "September," and then we have "August." That is the question I would like to clarify. I am not leading the witness anywhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I don't think the answer is very clear. There might be some confusion. You may ask your question again so that we could get a clear answer from this witness to make sure how many times those things happened. Yes, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just wanted to point out that the witness has answered two times. He said that first it took place in August. Upon Prosecutor's question whether it was in August or September, just as I was about to make my objection, the witness once again said that it happened in August. So I don't know what is still unclear there. We don't have to correct the witness three times about this date.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: What I have is --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Just a second, if I may, please. I was referring to the date when I crossed the line. I will tell you how it was. I believe that the exact date was the 18th of September, 1993. It was around 12.15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What happened on that day, from the very beginning, let's say -- I would like to hear from you about this date in very tight chronology, if you can, of course.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can. That morning between 6.00 and 7.00, just as any other morning, Stela's driver, Dinko, came to the sports hall at the Heliodrom. He was driving a blue Dais, a DM vehicle actually. He took 31 of us, just as he did every other morning, to take us to perform labour. He drove us to Stela's headquarters. And outside his headquarters, Stela lined us up, as was his custom, which was, of course, accompanied by all kinds of verbal abuse, name calling and so on and so forth, like extremists, fundamentalists. In the meantime, a person called Vladic, also known as Popaj, arrived, who used to work in the Auto-Moto company, which was then an HVO workshop. He needed four or five men to go to work there. But Stela said that he needed all of us there, that no one should go up there on that particular day. At that moment, soldiers began to arrive. And according to their accent, I think that those were people from the area of Ljubuski and Siroki Brijeg, the Western Herzegovina. They wanted us to clean their rifles, so I cleaned two rifles. After that, one of the soldiers, whose name I don't remember - I don't know who he was - --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stop. Okay, okay. I will ask you a specific question about prisoners who were taken together with you. So you should abstain from giving any names now. Okay. You may go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Okay, I understand. I won't mention any names. At that moment, we were taken back -- that is, I was returned to the line after I had cleaned those rifles. So I was again with all the others standing in a line against the wall, and we were made to crouch down. Stela gave us a quarter of a loaf of bread and a tin with some 400 grams of food; however, I wasn't able to eat the food because soon Stela arrived accompanied by Ernest Takac, also known as Brada. And he pointed his finger at four of us, and he said, "You, you, you, and you," and told us to go down to the cellar of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please wait a minute. Witness, do you know the names of prisoners who were singled out by Stela?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes, I do know the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour, we go into private session for some minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may go ahead. So you went to the basement, yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes. There was a very large table there, and Stela was sitting at that table. He called the four of us, and he told us to get dressed. In one of the corners of the room, there were some camouflage uniforms. At that moment, I asked -- because I had a premonition of some sorts that things were not going so well, so I asked him if we could do without it. But Stela told me to keep quiet and not to say anything but to get dressed. And he also said that whatever he says, the only thing we can say to that was, "Yes, sir. Yes, Colonel." Then we put on those uniforms. Brko called my name, and he told me to come close, and he said that I should be their commander. And he said, "Whatever I tell you, you have to convey the message to them," and so on. So I said, "Yes, sir. Yes, Colonel."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, I would like to clarify the name. It's not clear. Brko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes, at that time, I was wearing a moustache, and that's why he called me Brko, which means "the one wearing the mustachio."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your task?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: He told us that we had a task to accomplish, that we had some work to do, that the work consisted in crossing over the line, jumping into the trenches which were held by the BH army. And he said that as soon as we jumped in, we should seize the rifles of whoever happened to be in the trench. And he also said that they would follow us, they would come after us, and that we would all see each other there. After that, he said, "If you succeed in your mission, you will be released within 48 hours." So that was basically our task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get any ammunition for the fulfilment of your task?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Once we got out of the cellar, Marinko, whose surname I don't know, gave us rucksacks full of stones and bricks, and he also gave us some wooden rifles, wooden rifles which looked like the real ones. At that time, I was also given a bottle of engine oil by a soldier who shoved it in my left front shirt pocket, and said, "This is your Motorola." Then they took us to the red building and put us in a garage next to it, which did not have a door on it. A soldier brought us a pack of cookies and two litres of juice. We stayed there for about 15 minutes, maybe longer. I don't remember exactly how long. And then at one point, Ernest Takac, called Brada, arrived and told us to follow him, which is what we did. We followed him and finally arrived at the health centre. Once we got there, something exploded, a hand grenade, I think, just outside the building, and I was hit by a piece of glass in my right leg. We stayed there for about ten minutes until a T-55 tank arrived, which had some protection in the form of tyres and wooden planks. Takac simply said, "Go," and pushed us. So two of us ended up on the right side of the barrel of the tank and two others on the left side of the tank and also in front of the tank. As soon as we got there, the tank opened fire. Our heads were splitting from the detonations. All of a sudden, we were caught between -- in crossfire. The BH army was on one side and the HVO on the other. We didn't know what to do. I turned around, and I could see Takac looking at me. So I made a gesture with my hand like this, and I asked him what we should do, because we couldn't go back. But he simply waved his hand, which was supposed to mean "Just move on." We were about to reach the other side where there were some ruins of a building. Only walls were standing. And once again, the tank opened fire just above our heads, targeting the building. And then this whole wall fell on top of us, and we were covered with dust and rubble. One of us was severely wounded, one was wounded in his leg from the rubble. The first one that I told you about was wounded with a piece of shrapnel. I don't know exactly how long we stayed there, but I'm sure sometime between 15 minutes and half an hour. I could see behind my back -- that is, I could tell that I was being pushed by something, which was actually a rifle. I could see a rifle. Because I had actually shielded a loophole with my back. In the meantime, while we were there, two of us were hit by something in our heads; those were pieces of shrapnel. I was fully aware of the situation. I knew where I was, and I started to call out -- I started to shout, "Don't shoot. We're detainees." And I repeated this two or three times, after which the shooting somewhat subsided. And I was the first one to jump at one of the members of the BH army. As I was doing so, I was saying -- I was telling them not to shoot, that we were detainees. One of the three men who stayed behind followed me immediately. And then we asked this member of the BH army at whom we jumped to help us to pull the other two in because they were unable to do it themselves because they were wounded. However, he simply didn't dare do it. So I went back together with my colleague, and we helped the other two. We helped them get in. We pulled them inside, into the cellar of this building. And at that moment, a nurse appeared from somewhere and dressed our wounds. The two of us who were not so severely wounded went downstairs, and we filled the rifle clips with ammunition for the members of the BH army pursuant to their orders, because there was a very fierce attack by the HVO going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's stop at this point. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to go into private session for some minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness OO --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, Witness, I would like you to show me your target -- let's say the building you were supposed to reach, I mean on the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Our aim was to reach this building here, that is, to see whether there was anyone inside. Normally, BH army members were implied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe you can take the pointer and mark this building as number 1, as your target.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember at what time approximately did the tank appear in the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: The tank appeared around 10 to 12.00 or 15 to 12.00. I didn't have a watch. So around 10 to 15 minutes before 12.00, the tank appeared here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: At the time when the tank appeared, we were in this building here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Inside the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Inside. More precisely, in this corner here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Put number "2" on this place.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness OO, while inside the building of the medical centre, were you together with Stela's soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Only one soldier, actually, and that was Ernest Takac, nicknamed Brada, which means "a beard."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you show the route the tank was moving in the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark it with an arrow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: The tank was moving along this way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember at what time did you leave the building? I mean the four of you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I think it was about 10 or 15 past 12.00 a.m. -- p.m., sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show in this picture the way you were moving? I mean outside.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: We got to the health centre from this side, between -- going between these buildings. And at this point we entered the health centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after you were given command to leave the building and to be involved in the attack, to attack, let's say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: We left the building through this exit, going from this edge of the building, and we got to a point when we were standing just in front of the tank. Behind this little fountain, there was Stela's soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So could you explain to the Trial Chamber how were you moving with your wooden rifles? In what position did you -- were you holding your wooden rifles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: We held our rifles at the ready, soldier's fashion, so the rifles were slung around our necks and we held them with our hands at the ready.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I would like to know how were you moving in respect of Stela's soldiers. Do you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I don't think I understood your question sufficiently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You were given a command to attack. What happened after you were given this attack, command to attack, you left the building and you were, let's say, performing your task? What were you doing, and what were the others doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: We were pushed at the tank, and the tank started to fire. From the detonation, I was totally disoriented, and so were the others probably. Can you imagine being right next to the tank's barrel, perhaps half a metre away? You probably know what occurs in such a situation. Sorry. I had just come to, when I realised I was in the middle of the road, caught in crossfire. The road had two lanes, and I was somewhere in the middle. And also somewhere in the middle, one of the -- one of the street lights was broken into two. And that's where I was -- found myself standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the moment that some of your prison mates fell down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: The other inmates had been sent when we were already standing outside Stela's headquarters. They had already been given the task to remove the sandbags from the road, to let the tank pass. The sandbags were lined in the direction of the health centre on the road, this road. When I crossed over, I saw that there were many people dead, killed, HVO soldiers but also prisoners. I saw that people were panic-stricken and they were hauling the bodies, removing them to a place behind the fountain. And I had already mentioned that behind that fountain, Stela's soldiers were standing, as well as inmates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I would like you to mark this arrow with number "3" as the route of the tank.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you can show - or if you can't, you can't - the place you managed to reach when you crossed Bulevar. If you remember, of course.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I entered -- that entrance is here somewhere. I entered the building. I believe the building has three entranceways, and the one I used was somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's put number "4."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness OO --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: You may take away the exhibit now, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just informed the Trial Chamber that in the morning, they took 31 prisoners on that day. Do you know what happened to the rest of your prison mates on that day? Again, if you remember any names, please, let me know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: The remaining prisoners were wounded, and there were many people who were killed. Apart from myself, there were four relatives of mine. Out of those four, two were killed, one was wounded, and the fourth was unscathed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I ask for your permission to go into private session because otherwise, our witness's name and his relatives names will be revealed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did Stela and his soldiers treat prisoners who were working on the Bulevar, apart from this incident, of course, I mean, that happened in September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: They treated us this way and that, depending on the day. Sometimes they beat us. Sometimes they didn't. Sometimes they would give us more food than on other days. Cold and hard treatment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you observe any actual beating yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I personally was not beaten except for slapping me a bit or giving me a slight kick in passing. But I watched with my own eyes one incident which happened one day around 8.00 in the morning outside Stela's headquarters, that red building I had mentioned. We called that man "Professor." That's what everyone called him. I don't know either his first or his last name. He had greeted Stela with the words, "Hi, Vinko, how have you been? How's your father?" And he had told us before that he was on good terms with the man's father. Stela gave him a good beating which lasted for about two or three minutes. And after that, some of the soldiers took him behind the building where there was a fence, a small iron fence with garbage container. That's where they dumped him. He was alive at that point, but I don't know what became of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, my examination-in-chief is over. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll resume at 11.30 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Par:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. My name is Zelimir Par, and I'm an attorney at law representing, together with my colleague, Vinko Martinovic, Stela. I should like to ask you several questions regarding your testimony today.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated that you had been brought to Stela's unit on several occasions. Could you be more specific? How many times approximately were you brought there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: During the period of about 20 to 30 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean 20 or 30 occasions, because you would go back every day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the name of the unit once again, as you remember it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: The name of the unit was ATG Stela. Underneath there was the word "Mrmak" written on the insignia, after his dog.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The reason why I'm asking you this is because we have heard for the first time today that the name of the unit was Stela Mrmak. So far, the only testimonies that we heard, including one of the documents that I will mention later on, the name of the unit was only Mrmak. So is it because of the insignia that you remember the name of the unit, insignia which included both words?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Sir, I could see it with my own eyes. And in addition to that, I was a prisoner who wasn't even allowed to breathe, let alone observe things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that, Witness. But today you are testifying in your capacity as a witness, and I'm asking you as a witness to answer my questions. So let us stay within the framework of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You have to speak very slowly. We have difficulties to follow you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will slow down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, how many soldiers were there in this unit, according to your estimate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you move around in groups? Can you then tell us how many groups there were, at the times when you were assigned to those groups?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: No. I cannot tell you that, because sometimes the group would consist of four or five people to do the looting, and then another group would be working at the line. So we were basically scattered around, and I really couldn't tell you the approximate number of the soldiers in that unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let me now show you a map, the one that you already had in front of you, so that we can try and establish some other things in relation to this unit, with the help of this map, 14.5, please. I will give you a clean copy. Witness, using this photograph, could you point to us where the Bulevar was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I will tell you where I worked. And I worked at the Bulevar, so it would be here. This is the Health Centre and the area around it. This is where I worked. I already said that I'm not familiar with the town of Mostar because I am not a resident of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, that is precisely why I'm asking you the exact whereabouts of the Bulevar, because during your testimony, you stated that Stela was the commander of the Bulevar. What I'm trying to establish now, and in view of your lack of knowledge of the town of Mostar, what it is you meant by "Bulevar." The area that you just showed on the map, is that the area that you consider to be the Bulevar that you referred to during your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you then circle the area in question with a marker, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, so far from the testimony of other witnesses, we thought that the Bulevar was this line that is going across the photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: And that is exactly what I marked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the area that you have encircled, do you consider it to be the area of responsibility of Vinko Martinovic at the time you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My colleague has just drawn my attention to a hole in the circle. You haven't circled one part of the area, but we would like to know where the zone in question ends.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: There is an additional area up there, but I don't know exactly how far it stretched.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us now on either sides of the circle, were there any other units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: There were quite a few soldiers there, but I don't know what units they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. The interpreter didn't get the question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I don't know what units were there. But I know there was a large number of troops there. And that is the reason why I say this, because it was in this particular area that we worked, and there were some snipers' nests there, and there were lots of shelters and trenches all along the separation line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us go slowly. Were there any other units there? You said that there were many soldiers but you didn't know to which units they belonged.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you work for any other unit during your period in detention?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I have already said that I worked for the Croatian army, that I also worked at Rodoc for the commander there. I think it was the 9th Battalion. Working together with us at all times was also a man by the name of Darko. I don't know any other units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us stick to the photograph that is in front of you. My question concerned this particular photograph and the units that were deployed in the area depicted on the photograph. My question is very simple: Apart from the area that you have encircled, were you in any other unit that was perhaps deployed in an area which is shown on the photograph outside the circle; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Behind the building, which is marked as Sume Herceg-Bosna was the area where I worked for the Croatian army, but I don't know what the name of the neighbourhood is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are now looking at the photograph. On this photograph, do you recognise any other location where you worked, apart from the area around the health centre that you encircled? Is the building that you have just mentioned depicted on the photograph or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us turn to the separation line once again. On this photograph, could you point to us where the sides, where the two sides were deployed, that is, the BH army units, for example? Where were they deployed during the time you were there, and where exactly is the separation line with the BH army units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: The separation line is this road here, and the BH army forces were deployed -- I mean, at the time when I crossed the line, they were deployed in this partly destroyed building, in the cellars of this building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where is actually the separation line? Could you point to the separation line? Does the separation line consist only of this particular building, or does it stretch any further?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I know about this area here. This is what I observed at the time. And this is where the BH army units were. I don't know about any other positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us stick to the area that you have encircled for a while, and let us go back to the health centre. You do recognise the building, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us about the entrances and exits on the building? Where were the doors? Where could you enter and leave the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I entered the building from this side here and left it here at this edge, at the corner of the building, because the prisoners who were there before me had put some sandbags there, so there was some protection in the form of sandbags, and this particular spot was protected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have mentioned the sandbags. Where exactly did you see them? Where were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: You mean at the health centre?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: The sandbags were inside the building, at the windows and alongside the walls.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the area outside, near the road? Were there any sandbags there, and where exactly were they? Could you mark that for us, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: The sandbags were here approximately. I'm not sure I can be precise, but that is approximately the area where they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us stick to the entrances and exits to the building. You have mentioned two such exits. What about this front side, the front part near the fountain? Was there any door there? Was it possible to enter the building from that side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I could not see that because of the sandbags. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A witness who testified in open session, Allan Knudsen, stated that there was a door in the middle of the building through which the soldiers had withdrawn during the attack. Do you remember any such event? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Sir, I was about to be -- meet my death. I just cannot remember that door and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I fully understand that you are one of the victims of this war. However, today, you are a witness. You are safe and sound. Stela is in detention, and there is a number of things that need to be clarified from a different perspective. My questions are very simple, and I would appreciate if you could give me equally simple answers. So once again, I'm fully aware of the fact that you are one of the victims of the war, but we are now dealing with a different issue now. We are still dealing with this map, and a topic that we started, that is, whether Stela was the commander of the overall Bulevar area. According to your knowledge, can we agree with the fact that he was the commander of the area that you have marked with the circle here; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: The area from where I crossed over to the other side, that is the area where I worked on several occasions for Stela, who was the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us now turn to the event that you told us about. Do you know whether Stela was in command on that day, whether he was commanding the action that was taking place on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have a document here which states that the commander of the action in question was Mario Milicevic, Baja. Does the name ring a bell? Did you at any point in time during that day hear about him? Do you want me to show you this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: No, I don't know that. I'm not familiar with that fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, you stated that the action began around noon, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I said before noon, sometime before 12.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Because I saw the time on Ernest Takac's watch. He had a very good watch. The bracelet was silver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was according to that watch that --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: And he told us specifically that the artillery will become operative before our departure. And it is true that we couldn't hear anything because of the noise made by all those artillery pieces. And there was a lot of dust as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was how you knew what time it was, and you answered my question. The reason I asked you was because we had a witness whose pseudonym was NN who stated that the action had began around 5.00 a.m. How do you comment on that? Would that have been possible? Is it an action that perhaps lasted from 5.00 a.m. onwards? How do you respond to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I know that while we were still in front of Stela's command, there was no shooting. And that at one point in time, we got to the Health Centre and still there was no shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what time it was when you were brought there from the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: We left the Heliodrom between 6.00 and 7.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time, you didn't hear any shooting, any fire, from artillery pieces or anything of the sort, so you would not agree with that witness, the witness who stated that the action started at 5.00?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us now turn to the issue of so-called wooden rifles. Did you personally take part in the making of those rifles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: No. The rifles were made by one of the prisoners whose name was Huskovic. He was from Mostar. He was a carpenter by occupation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally see Huskovic making those rifles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I saw him paint the last rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When and where did you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I saw it the morning when we were outside Stela's command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know this person Huskovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: No, I met him in prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know he was a carpenter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see him again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you know that what he was working on was the last rifle, the last piece of rifle. Where were other rifles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Out of those four rifles, I saw the last one, that is, the last butt of the rifle as he was brushing it outside Stela's command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question concerned your personal knowledge, and you said no. My next question is whether any of those who you said carried those rifles had taken part in the making of those rifles.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The witness by the name of Knudsen who testified in open session on the 13th and 14th of November stated that he had personally seen that those were the same detainees, that is, that the same detainees had made the rifles and then carried those rifles during the action.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know any man by the name of Knudsen or any other foreign --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object again to this line of questioning. The witness is responsible for his own facts, for his own story. He can't be responsible for some story told by some other witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par. You should rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can rephrase the question, Mr. President. Of course, I'm not saying that the witness is responsible for somebody else's story. We all have the same objective here, and that is to establish the truth. I don't think that we will be doing anything wrong if we present the witness with some of the facts that have been described in different terms before this Chamber. But I can move on, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: First of all, we have to make sure whether there is only one incident involving the wooden rifle or if there were several such kinds of incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So far, my understanding has been that there was only one such incident. But I will bear that in mind, and I will try to clarify the issue with the help of this witness. But I do accept the objection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, on that day, on that particular occasion, during the event involving wooden rifles and yourself personally, did you personally see any foreign mercenary in the vicinity of your group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I was not able to observe such a thing, because the four of us were separated immediately, and I told you that we were first put in that garage, which we left, accompanied by Takac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, then. Let us now try to clarify the issue that Their Honours have pointed to. Did you, at any point in time, hear that anyone else, apart from the four of you, was exposed to death while carrying such wooden rifles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: No, not until that occasion, nor did I hear such a thing after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you whether you saw any foreign mercenaries. And I'm coming back to the testimony of that man because according to his testimony, you were sitting with the group of soldiers just before the operation started. And you are telling me that you -- the four of you were isolated and you were only together with Takac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: We were sitting with the rest of the group up until the moment when we put on the camouflage uniforms, and once we had put them on, we were taken out to the garage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Par, the questioning or the cross-examination of this witness appears to me to suggest that Mr. Knudsen and other witnesses are talking about the same incident as this witness, and I believe that the testimony which we have heard suggests that there were several - maybe on the same day - but groups of people who were exposed to crossfire in similar circumstances. And if you carefully read the notes of the other witnesses' evidence, you'll find that there may have been several groups of such detainees. Otherwise, I don't want to interrupt your cross-examination, but you must be fair to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand what you're saying, Your Honour, and I understood the testimony of other witnesses. But my cross-examination of this witness today regards only the wooden rifles and the group of four prisoners who were carrying those wooden rifles, and I'm trying to establish the position of this witness, who was a protagonist of this event, and to compare it with the testimony of other people who claimed they had carried wooden rifles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Well, that would be perfectly valid for you to do that, and that is what a competent lawyer must do. The only thing is that the description of the incident as given to us by Mr. Knudsen was that the prisoners were actually in a different building, so they couldn't be the same group. And also, they were with soldiers from Mr. Stela's unit, a number of soldiers, not just Ernest Takac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. I really don't want to dwell on this and bother this Trial Chamber any more, but I'm coming to the part when Knudsen said he saw prisoners with wooden rifles. But let's move on. I think we've clarified this in a way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, let us go back to that room where you were waiting for the start of the operation and where the four of you were singled out, as you said. This is the moment when you already have these wooden rifles on you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there in that room any trunks with ammunition, stretchers, anything like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that day, in the course of the operation and on a different occasion, did you see any prisoners carrying cases with ammunition, using laths for carrying such trunks? Did you see anything like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: You mean while I was in prison?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean on that day, when you were around that unit, when you were coming or going.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: On that day, I didn't have occasion to see anything like it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But generally speaking, did you see any prisoners carrying ammunition, stretchers to the positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Do you mean that day?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Generally speaking. Have you ever seen that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I had a job to do that day. I was cleaning RPGs and other rifles. It was a normal occurrence in prison. Even explosives were carried by prisoners, and they were made to set explosives to certain buildings, things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why am I asking this? How were these cases with ammunition carried? Did you see prisoners carrying these cases using some laths that they put underneath the case in order to lift it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About these rifles, in view of the fact that we have heard different descriptions so far, what colour were the rifles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: With the Court's permission, the rifles were black. And I still have that rifle today. I'm sorry I didn't bring it here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean you have it still today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Precisely. It was placed in a museum in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We are very interested to see this rifle. I wonder whether the Prosecution could do something to bring it here as evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will try.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, how do you intend to show us that it is, indeed, that rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: By bringing it. How could I prove it otherwise?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean, how can you prove it is that rifle? How can you prove that it wasn't made on a different occasion by AID, for instance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I will bring at least 50 witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I object. The witness isn't supposed to prove anything in this courtroom. He is supposed to give his testimony. Why should he prove that such kind of wood rifle belonged to someone else or it was the same rifle that was used in September?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Par, we believe that the witness has already answered your question. No matter whether you like it or not, you have to take it. That was his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. With your leave, I thought I was entitled to question him about the circumstances in which he got hold of that rifle which he kept. I thought I could question the witness about the veracity of his claim, but the Court is now prohibiting me from doing that, if I understood you correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: This witness said that not only would he be able to tell you what colour the rifle was but he had the rifle. Now, I would agree that that evidence took everyone by surprise. And generally speaking, we don't approve of surprises. But these things happen in cross-examination. He then said that he could bring the rifle. And you said, "How do we know? How do you know it wasn't made by AID or someone else?" And this witness then said it was the rifle he had. And I suppose that is the end of the matter, because one is bound by the answers that one makes in cross-examination. You can bring another witness to say that that is not the rifle because the rifles that were made on that day were brown or yellow. It isn't open to you to say it was made by AID.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Honourable Judge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, would you then answer this question: Will you bring that rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: If the competent authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina approve another trip to The Hague and back and pay for my travel expenses, I can bring that rifle any time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, Witness, what are those competent authorities whose approval you need? If you need that, we can go into private session.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: There's no need for that. Those are the competent agencies of the Federation's army, because I am a soldier of the Federation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If they are to approve it, you need to tell them the precise reason for that trip.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: That's true. I have no problem coming here whatsoever because Bosnia and Herzegovina has signed a document in cooperation with the Tribunal in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I meant is do you need to familiarise them with the substance of what you are supposed to do here? Do you need to inform them of that, considering that you're a military man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I have -- I don't have any difficulty talking to them, and I don't have any difficulty in coming here as a witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have to know this, Witness: Do you need to tell your superiors before you come here again, "I need to go to The Hague once again in order to bring the rifle"? That's what I meant by "substance."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: No. I need just a piece of paper from this Tribunal, and this will become possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. I'm skipping further questions about the rifle because we are probably going to see it anyway. Have you kept even that rucksack which had been filled with rocks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: No, I don't have the rucksack, and I don't have the empty bottle of engine oil.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I dumped them in the middle of the road by the broken lamppost, and a part of that lamppost is still standing today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you throw away the rifle as well? Do you consider it to be of value?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I had no time. I was running, and I didn't even bother to carry that -- and the rucksack fell on its own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't you care in that situation whether you had it or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I was dressed up to play a human shield, and I was made to look as if I were attacking, and I was attacking with a wooden rifle. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So my question was about why you didn't throw away the rifle. Did you consider it to be dangerous at the moment, or you simply didn't give it any thought at the time, or you kept it on purpose? Can you answer that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I had no time to think, and God knows what went through my head at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Being where we are with the rucksack, the rifle, the Bulevar, I want to ask you this: You said that you were playing a sort of human shield.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: It was not a sort of. It was a human shield.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you then explain, please: You were acting as human shield. Who were you shielding with your body, which is what a human shield is supposed to do? Were you standing in front of a soldier or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: We were shielding both the tank and the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, how were you supposed to shield the tank? How did you do that? Explain.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I've already told you that we approached the tank, two from the right, two from the left, and we were standing half a metre away from the barrel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understood that part. That is a position in which I can imagine the tank shielding you, not other way around.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Come on, sir, please. That's not how it was. That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you shielding some particular soldiers? Were any soldiers running, walking behind you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Behind the fountain, there was Ernest Takac and other soldiers. I've already said this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But we are now dealing with the issue of human shield. When I hear "human shield," I imagine a live body protecting somebody who is standing behind him. Was that the case with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I've described to you the task that we were given. I told you that we were standing in front of a T-55 tank. I told you that Takac and other soldiers were behind the fountain. I don't know what you're thinking. I can only know what I think. I was a human shield, propped up to die, and I'm proud that I survived and that I'm able to tell the truth here for the sake of all those who died.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I thought we had agreed to work by questions and answers. I'll explain to you why I'm asking this. I'm asking because we've heard a number of witnesses testify that they -- the soldiers were moving right behind the prisoners carrying wooden rifles. Was it the case with you? That's the only thing I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I don't understand you. I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll try to make it clearer. Let us look at this map. Can we draw, again on this map, where the tank was when -- where you were and where the soldiers were relative to you? Were HVO soldiers shielded by your bodies, or were they elsewhere, on another side of the tank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: The soldiers were behind the fountain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So draw it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I have already drawn it. The soldiers were behind the fountain. I've shown to you where the sandbags were. I've shown where the tank was. I've shown to you where I was standing and where I made the crossing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: That's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Let us, then, go back to this assignment you were given. As far as I understood, you said you were given this assignment by Stela, in the basement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the assignment was given, you were told that if you succeed, you would be released, let go; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes, within 48 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of any case during that day when prisoners volunteered to participate in the operation of pulling out the wounded and dead bodies, wherein if they succeed, they would be released, allowed even to go to third countries? Do you know of any such case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I had already crossed over. I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: And if you want to ask some questions about -- in this direction, we could go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll ask my question without mentioning the name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That person that we just mentioned, did he maybe volunteer to participate in that operation of pulling out HVO soldiers dead or alive? Was that possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Sir, that same person you're talking about pulled out the dead body of our common relative from the area around the fountain. I think it's now perfectly clear why he volunteered, even if he volunteered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Who issued orders to you in that operation? Was it Takac or was it Stela? Did you see Stela at all on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I saw Stela when he was giving us that assignment in the basement, and Takac was the one who took us to the health centre. I've already told you all of this before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. While we are talking about this, did I understand you correctly as saying that you got those wooden rifles and rucksacks after you got out of the basement, when you left Stela, not while you were in his presence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes. We got them after we got out of the basement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One more thing regarding the operation. You are together with Takac getting out towards the tank. At the moment when you got out, was there any shooting, or did it start later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: We didn't get out. That's not the right word. Ernest Takac was pushing us, pushing me personally, and there was shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at the moment when you were getting out, you heard shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: We were not getting out. We were being pushed out. Those are two different concepts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm saying again, we had another witness testify that there was no shooting at that moment. Can you tell us, what was that shooting from? Was it artillery fire? Was it other shooting that put you in danger?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: At that moment, there was fire from mortars positioned on Bijeli Brijeg. I know very well where Bijeli Brijeg is. The full range of artillery; it was a rainfall. Everything was firing at that moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that, sir. Was it immediately from the Bulevar, from -- was there any shooting from the side of the BH army which could have threatened your life while you were getting out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: There was shooting; I don't know from which side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. When you crossed over, the fact that you crossed over, was it part of the assignment given you by Stela, or was it already escape? Did you simply decide at one point when you got out to cross over to the other side at the point where you showed us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Naturally I was happy to be alive, to have survived. Probably I wouldn't have survived if I had to stay in those dungeons, because those were dungeons honestly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can believe me if I say I'm glad you survived. I'm saying this in all honesty. My question was, however: Did you decide to make a run for it at one point, or was it part of the assignment that was given you? In other words, was there an understanding among the four of you to take your chances and make a run for it at one point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: No, there was no planning involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in order to come to the end of this tragic day of the 17th, can I ask you to mark two or three points on the map again. You were indisposed to do that earlier, but could you please do it. Kindly could you draw the place where the tank was, where you were standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I marked where the tank was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Put number "2" where you were, to mark your position. And please put number "3" where the other soldiers were standing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you draw an interrupted line from the tank to the place where you -- which you eventually reached.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, just another interrupted line from the exit you used to the tank.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We don't need the photograph any longer. We'll move to another topic. And this topic is the Professor. There was a prisoner nicknamed Professor. And in your presence, he was beaten up one day. That was your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever find out the name of that man? Did you know it on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I never learned his name. And I didn't really try to learn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could there have been two prisoners with the same nickname Professor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS OO
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
